title: Runbook
description: AIP schema for runbook-style Instructions: a workflow with trigger conditions, applicability contexts, steps, signal-to-action decisions, integrations, and worked examples. Scope is the category of work (any runbook), not a specific skill.

purpose.description: One- or two-sentence statement of what this runbook does and why.

trigger_when.description: Conditions under which the agent should consider this skill. Mixed granularity is expected: immediate triggers ("user asks 'add X'") and broader applicability contexts ("evaluating technology choices") belong in the same list. Matches the single-field convention used by Anthropic Agent Skills, MCP, and OpenAI tool definitions.

scope_and_approval.description: Read-only vs write actions, approval checkpoints, constraints. Freeform prose.

steps.description: Ordered workflow steps the agent executes.

parallel.description: True if sub-tasks within the step run in parallel.

one_of.description: Mutually exclusive sub-steps; the agent picks exactly one.

modes.description: Optional execution modes (e.g., quick inline vs full subagent). Each item is a named mode with a freeform body.

name.description: Short identifier for the mode (e.g., quick, full).

search_shortcuts.description: Reference list of common tools, libraries, or services grouped by category. Each item is a category with a freeform body.

body.description: Items in the category as freeform prose.

integrations.description: How this runbook composes with other agents, skills, or workflows. Each item is a partner with a freeform body so sub-structure (sub-bullets, cycles, etc.) is preserved.

partner.description: Name of the partner agent, skill, or workflow.

body.description: How the integration works, as freeform prose.

examples.description: Worked examples showing the runbook applied to concrete cases.

search.description: The search query or queries used (optional).
